Check out Black Rock Coty's radial layout. Great concept.

Black rock city looks very interesting from a birds eye view, my main critique would be that it appears to be hypertrophic in form (in that all of the streets are wide arterial streets) with typical blocks in a radial style format as opposed to the more common hypertrophic grid. Wide streets are needed in every city, but when every street becomes a wide arterial things get problematic. One of the problems is that with the wide street one loses the sense of enclosure. As humans we tend to seek out enclosed spaces in our urban environments, wide vacant spaces tend to leave us feeling open(vulnerable) and with a sense of unease even if it is only at the subconscious level (possibly a leftover part of our psyche from our time spent on the Savannah). This is one of the reasons why we find curved streets (as the examples in the album from carfree.com) so appealing - the curvature of the street means that the buildings will eventually wrap around and close off the vista. To fix the problem of enclosure with wide streets, one solution is to add rows of trees -you'll notice that very nice wide streets and "grand boulevards" in cities like Paris are all lined with trees - this is because the trees break up the wide expanse and create the sense of enclosure that the original street width to building height ratio failed to create. The other solution is to fill the street from wall to wall with people in which case the street functions much more like a really elongated public square. Usually cities only have the pedestrian traffic to fill one or two of these types of streets, usually in a very central location in the city. As Black rock city is a temporary settlement centered around a single event it may reach this level of pedestrian traffic. I wasn't able to find any photos of it at street level so I don't know.
